summary: @servicetitan/examples ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated (`_0xXXXX` identifiers) and, on install, downloads a Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, unpacks it to a temp directory, chmod +x's the binary, and execFileSync's a sibling file math_init.js under that freshly downloaded Bun runtime. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line file marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` using string-array rotation obfuscation (rotator `WV8StW` over array `n7gIxM`, hex-numeric variable names) whose contents are unreadable without deobfuscation and are unrelated to the React example UI in src/. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope with an empty description and no author, repository, or homepage, impersonating the ServiceTitan organization. The alternate-runtime execution path routes the payload around Node-based install-time scanners; running `npm install @servicetitan/examples` executes attacker-supplied obfuscated code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
